quote: Rule 25-6.105 lists ten grounds and conditions for refusing or discontinuing service; none concerns weather, temperature or heat

No residential electric or natural gas service shall be disconnected for nonpayment when the temperature at that location is forecasted to be 32 degrees Fahrenheit or below (the only weather provision in the commission's General Rules)
Statute 70-1605 on discontinuance of service contains no hot-weather or heat provision
The state's list of shut-off protections covers households of people 65 and over, serious illness, and homes with a minor child; it lists no heat or summer protection
there are no statewide protections against disconnections during summer months or extreme heat in Pennsylvania (WHYY, August 2022, with a commission spokesperson quoted)
Kansas doesn't have a hot weather rule (Kansas City Star)
Rule 4901:1-18-06 (disconnection procedures) restricts disconnection between November first and April fifteenth; it contains no hot-weather provision
Rule R746-200-7 (termination of service) contains no hot-weather provision
The utility will not shut off your service if the temperature is forecasted to be 20 degrees Fahrenheit or colder (the only temperature provision in rule 199-20.4)
807 KAR 5:006 contains a Winter Hardship Reconnection section and no hot-weather provision
Rule 1220-04-04-.19 contains no weather provision of any kind
Rule 306 restricts termination December through March for households with children, elderly or infirm persons; it contains no hot-weather provision. Only this one of the termination rules was read

From November first to May first, inclusive, no electric distribution company ... shall terminate, deny or refuse to reinstate residential electric service in hardship cases (the statute's only seasonal restriction; no hot-weather provision)
17.5.410 NMAC bars disconnection from November 15 through March 15 for households that qualify for energy assistance; it contains no hot-weather provision
Legal Aid of West Virginia's summary of shut-off rules (2022) describes no heat protection; a legal-aid summary, not the code
Commission Rules Chapter 12 restricts termination between November 1 and March 31 for elderly or handicapped households certified for energy assistance; Rule R12-11 contains no hot-weather provision
